title: Entangling Topological Invariants
abstract: An isolated occupied multiplet may admit local tensor-product descriptions without a globally consistent subsystem structure. We characterize the obstruction by comparing the transition functions of the occupied multiplet with those generated by independent basis changes in the two candidate subsystems. When a decomposition into rank-one sectors over a closed surface is specified, the resulting quotient removes row- and column-additive Chern data and yields mixed Chern classes. Momentum-dependent mixing of the sector labels adds the Gauss--Codazzi curvature of the moving lines, while in the label-conserving limit the mixed class is measured by a crossed Thouless pump. When only the factor dimensions $p$ and $q$ are specified, the comparison is made at the level of the clutching map of a rank-$pq$ bundle over $S^4$. Product frames generate winding numbers in $q\mathbb Z+p\mathbb Z$, so global factorization is possible exactly when $C_2$ is divisible by $\gcd(p,q)$; in particular, odd $C_2$ obstructs a $2\times2$ factorization. We illustrate the two settings with finite eight-level Hamiltonians and give pumping and occupied-projector tomography protocols for their readout.
summary: This work develops a sophisticated topological framework to measure entanglement in electronic systems by quantifying obstructions to factorizing the occupied state manifold. It shows that while local measurements might suggest independent subsystems, global invariants like mixed Chern classes reveal genuine, non-factorizable quantum correlations. This has direct implications for understanding exotic topological phases in condensed matter physics.
main_problem: The core problem is characterizing topological obstructions that prevent the global factorization of occupied electronic multiplets when decomposing them into independent candidate subsystems.
main_result: The mixed Chern class ($\chi$) successfully isolates non-factorizable topological information, and a specific criterion based on $\gcd(p,q)$ determines if global factorization is possible over $S^4$.
method: The authors use algebraic topology tools, comparing transition functions via quotient structures (like the subsystem-gluing quotient) and analyzing clutching maps for bundles over $S^4$.
model_or_system: The study concerns isolated occupied multiplets described by vector bundles ($E 	o X$) in multiband quantum systems, analyzed using Hamiltonians and spectral projectors.
key_observables: Mixed Chern classes ($\chi_{ab}$), total/one-label Chern numbers ($C_{tot}, C_A, C_B$), charge transfers ($\Delta Q$), and the clutching quotient $\eta_{p,q}(E)$.
important_parameters: The factor dimensions $p$ and $q$, the geometry of the underlying manifold (e.g., closed surface vs. $S^4$), and the flux pumping parameters.
main_assumptions: The analysis relies on defining appropriate quotient structures to filter out trivially factorizable topological data, and in some cases, assumes ideal measurement protocols for tomography.
figures_summary: Figures illustrate that while total and one-label responses vanish (e.g., $\Delta Q_{tot} = \Delta Q_A = 0$), the mixed invariant ($\chi$) remains nonzero, confirming entanglement beyond simple factor contributions.
paper_structure: The paper progresses from defining the obstruction via transition function comparison on a general surface to analyzing the specific case of $S^4$ using clutching maps. It then applies these concepts to physical measurements like flux pumping and projector tomography protocols.
why_interesting: It provides rigorous mathematical tools (mixed Chern classes, clutching quotients) to quantify entanglement in topological quantum matter that cannot be captured by simply summing up contributions from individual subsystems.
